1.0.0.en: 1 The oracle of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi. 2 "I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob, 3 And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the wolves of the wilderness. 4 Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the LORD of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever. 5 And your eyes shall see, and ye shall say, The LORD will be magnified from the border of Israel.

1.0.1.en: The oracle of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi: [1]

1.0.2.en: Some translate the word "oracle" here as "burden." For Israel in its wickedness, the word of the Lord did not represent joy, gladness and sweetness, because it uncovered their wounds without flattery. Therefore they counted it a burden upon them, which grieved them so that they were unable to hear it. It is a burden to the one who does not seek the salvation of his soul, but those who are earnest about the salvation of their souls find it an easy and sweet yoke (Mt 11:30).

1.0.3.en: I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us?

1.1.0.en: Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD, yet I loved Jacob [2].

1.1.1.en: Since this book reveals the calling of all the nations and peoples to accept the faith, it begins by affirming God's love for His people, freely and without any merit on their part. Yet they made light of His love, despised His name and defiled the offerings and sacrifices. For this reason God no longer took pleasure in them as long as they walked in this way, and He opens the door to all the nations, from the rising of the sun to its going down, that His name may be glorified in all the earth.

1.1.2.en: He began to open the wounds of His people in order to cleanse and treat them, assuring them that He does this not out of hatred or enmity but out of love and tenderness. For this reason God's message to them begins with the words: "I have loved you." This is what God has affirmed continually through His prophets: "Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee" (Jer 31:3). "When Israel was a child, then I loved him" (Hos 11:1), "for the LORD delighteth in thee" (Isa 62:4).

1.1.3.en: Thus He begins His speech by declaring His love, to affirm that if He rebukes, it is because He is a Father: "As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten" (Rev 3:19). He rebukes them because they did not return love for love.

1.1.4.en: Man needs someone who loves him and who receives his love. That is why God so often assures His children: "I have loved you." But when circumstances that seem harsh and bitter in his eyes pass over a man, he asks within himself: "Where is God's love for me?"

1.1.5.en: They doubted His love for them and made light of it: "Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us?" By saying this they belittle God's love and His care for them.

1.1.6.en: "Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD, yet I loved Jacob" [2]. The Jews often think that God is bound to love them because they are the sons of Abraham, and that He repays them with love as one who is in debt to their father. Therefore He says to them: if I loved you in return for Abraham's love for Me, then Esau should have enjoyed My love more than Jacob, for he was the firstborn; yet Jacob seized the love of God by practical faith, while Esau fell under wrath by the hardness of his heart. God's love is not based on partiality, nor on mere bodily kinship, for Esau and Jacob were twin brothers in one womb, and Jacob enjoyed entering into a covenant with God, while Esau deprived himself of the gift.

1.1.7.en: This gift that Jacob received was free; he had no merit in it. It is according to God's good pleasure, but not by compulsion or force; rather it comes through man's response to the free divine grace.

1.1.8.en: * God foreknows sinful people while they are yet in their mothers' wombs (Gen 25:23).

1.1.9.en: * "The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies" (Ps 58:3)... What is this? Let us examine it more attentively, for perhaps he says this because God foreknew the men who are sinners while they were in their mothers' wombs. Therefore, when Rebecca was still with child, having conceived twins, it was said: "Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated" (Mal 1:2; Rom 9:13). For it was said: "The elder shall serve the younger." God's judgment was hidden at that time, but from the womb, from the very origin, sinners go astray. From what do they go astray? From the truth. From what do they go astray? From the blessed city, from the blessed life.

1.1.10.en: St. Augustine * Cain despised his brother, as he despised God. How did he despise Him? By his impudent answer to God: "Am I my brother's keeper?" (Gen 4:9). Esau despised his brother, and he too despised God. Therefore God said: "Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated" (Rom 9:13; Mal 1:2-3).

1.1.11.en: St. John Chrysostom * We think rightly when we say that "God loves justice and hates robbery by injustice." This does not mean that He has a leaning toward the one or the other, and accepts what is opposed, to the point of preferring this and not preferring that. For that is the characteristic of creatures. Rather it means that, as a judge, He loves the righteous and helps them, and turns away from the wicked.

1.1.12.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic God declared His love for Israel, saying: "When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt" (Hos 11:1), for He called him a child and His son. Without partiality, when the people of Israel persisted in their evils, His prophet St. John the Baptist calls them: "O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?" (Mt 3:7). Thus there is no partiality with God!

1.1.13.en: * It is the fruit of their folly and their childish thinking that they suffer this punishment. I called them out of Egypt and freed them from harsh bondage, but they showed ingratitude to Me and chose the worship of idols. I who taught them to walk, and healed them of their hideous conduct, and showed them fatherly tenderness, and used every kind of remedy with them, they refused to know Me, although I had preserved them from a double destruction at the hands of the invaders. They are like those who have fastened their nails into Me, and I love them as though that were a chain.

1.1.14.en: Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus * Israel was called a son symbolically from the time he was in Egypt (Mt 2:15), but he lost his sonship by worshipping Baal and offering incense to idols, so John gave them a name fitting them, "generation of vipers" (Mt 3:7). Since they lost the title of sonship that was poured out upon them through grace in the days of Moses, they received from John a name that matched their deeds.

1.2.0.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains waste, and his heritage for the wolves of the wilderness? [3]

1.2.1.en: Edom (Esau) defied the God of Israel and cared nothing for His divine will, so in due time he fell into everlasting ruin. Israel, on the other hand, who was under chastening, received the blessing of the revelation of God's glory within his borders. This work goes on continually in the spiritual realm. If a Jew or a Gentile defies the God of hosts, he becomes like a spiritual Edom; God is long-suffering toward him, and when his cup is filled with evil he falls into eternal destruction. Meanwhile many of the Gentiles who were the stubborn spiritual Edom, when they return to the Lord, become the new Israel, filled with divine glories.

1.2.2.en: Esau was violent with his brother, his father and his mother, so he married two daughters of Heth, "which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah" (Gen 26:35). He drank of the cup that he had filled for his parents and his brother, so ruin befell his heart, and this ruin turned back even upon the mountains of Seir, which were "his heritage." The army of the Chaldeans came and laid them waste until they became a dwelling for the wolves of the wilderness, having become utterly desolate.

1.2.3.en: The sons of Esau, or the sons of Edom, who rejoiced at the destruction of Jerusalem (Ps 137:7), drank from the very cup of staggering that they had filled for others.

1.2.4.en: God was very long-suffering toward Edom and left it generation after generation, so that some thought that God's threats against them were only words without action. But at last it fell into perpetual ruin, and there has been no kingdom of Edom since.

1.2.5.en: * Rebecca carried the two, Jacob and Esau. The seed is one, but the two who were conceived are different. The womb is one, and the two she carried are different. Did not the free woman conceive Esau? They struggled together within their mother's womb, there they quarreled, and it was said to Rebecca: "Two nations are in thy womb"; two men, two nations, yet they struggled in the womb. How many wicked people there are in the Church! One womb conceives them until they are separated in the end, and the wicked cry out against the good, and both struggle in the bowels of their one mother.

1.2.6.en: * Who is so foolish and wicked as to say that God is unable to change the evil will of men, however He wishes, whenever He wishes and wherever He wishes, and make it good? But when He works, He works through mercy; and when He does not work, it is through justice. For "he hath mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth" (Rom 9:18). Now when the Apostle said this, he was praising grace, which he spoke of when he connected it with the twins in Rebecca's womb. "For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth; it was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger" (Rom 9:11-12). Consequently he points to another prophetic testimony, where it is written: "Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated" (Mal 1:2-3). And since he realized how what he had said might cause disturbance to those whose understanding could not enter into this depth of grace, he added: "What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid" (Rom 9:14). And yet it seems that, unjustly, without any merit from good or evil works, God loves one and hates the other. Now if the Apostle had wished us to understand that there were future good works of the one, which God had doubtless foreknown, he would not have said: "Not of works" (Rom 9:11), but he would have said: "from future works." Thus he wished to resolve the difficulty; or rather, he wished not to leave a difficulty to be resolved. For he added at once: "God forbid" (to show that there is no unrighteousness in God). "For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion" (Rom 9:15). Now who but a fool thinks there is unrighteousness in God, whether when He inflicts a penalty on one who deserves it, or shows mercy to one who does not deserve it? Finally the Apostle concludes by saying: "So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy" (Rom 9:16).

1.2.7.en: St. Augustine * From the beginning of the world, of the two sons born to Adam, Abel the younger was chosen, while Cain the elder, being a type of the unbelieving Jews, was condemned. Afterward, in the time of Abraham, the same type was fulfilled in Sarah and Hagar. Sarah was barren for a long time as a type of the Church, while Hagar, as a type of the Jewish synagogue, conceived a son at once. Here the younger son, Isaac, was received into the inheritance, while Ishmael the elder was deprived of it. This truth appears to be fulfilled in the two: Jacob the younger was loved by God, while Esau was rejected, as it is written: "Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated" (Mal 1:2-3). This type is also known to be fulfilled in the two sisters whom Jacob took as wives: Rachel the younger, whom Jacob loved more than Leah the elder. In fact, from the former was born Joseph, who was sold into Egypt as a type of our Lord and Savior. So Leah was weak of sight, while Rachel was beautiful in form; this too has a meaning: Leah is understood as the synagogue of the Jews, and Rachel points to the Church. A man whose bodily eyes are inflamed cannot look upon the brightness of the sun. So the synagogue, whose heart's eyes were filled with envy and malice against our Lord and Savior, as with a flood filled with poison, cannot look upon the loftiness of Christ, who is the Sun of righteousness (Mal 4:2).

1.2.8.en: Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places.

1.2.9.en: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down.

1.3.0.en: And they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever. [4]

1.3.1.en: Edom thought that it was able by itself to rise from this ruin that had come upon it, without reforming the heart and driving out the wolves within. Edom fell into vain hopes, and they thought they could rebuild the desolate places, as happened with Jerusalem.

1.3.2.en: By saying "we will return and build the desolate places," they see that the matter is in their own hands and depends on their military capabilities and their planning, whether God wills it or not. Therefore "thus saith the LORD of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down." For they cannot stand in defiance before God.

1.3.3.en: By their defiance they become an example and a warning to souls that exalt themselves against God. "And they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever" [4]. All understand the words of Job: "Who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?" (Job 9:4).

1.3.4.en: When the Jews rejected the Lord Christ and opposed His Gospel and His Church, they became Edomites, and this saying was fulfilled in them, for when they tried to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem in the days of the Emperor Hadrian, God demolished what they had built, by an earthquake and the bursting forth of tongues of fire, so that they were forced to stop building.

1.3.5.en: * If God uttered a thousand words accusing us, we would not be able to answer a single one. What does the prophet say? "In thy sight shall no man living be justified" (Ps 143:2).

1.3.6.en: St. John Chrysostom * "I acknowledge my sin to You, my God, and You have lifted away the iniquity of my heart" (cf. Ps 32:5). I do not dispute with You the judgment, O Truth, for I do not wish to deceive myself, lest my iniquity stand against me.

1.3.7.en: St. Augustine And your eyes shall see, and ye shall say:

1.4.0.en: The LORD will be magnified from the border of Israel. [5]

1.4.1.en: Since the heart of Edom became a wasteland, with no trace of love in it, but bearing the malice of wolves, its mountains turned to ruin and its heritage became the property of the wolves of the wilderness. Now that Israel, under chastening, asks for divine intervention, God is glorified in his borders as He is glorified in his inner depths. This is God's good pleasure, that the whole world become the new, spiritual Israel, bearing the glory of God within and without.

1.4.2.en: The Word of God came to transfer us, through Baptism, from sonship to the enemy of good to sonship to God, and to change us from the Edom that bears the barren, wolfish heart into the new Israel that bears the divine glory.

1.5.0.en: A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master.

1.5.1.en: If then I be a father, where is mine honour?

1.5.2.en: And if I be a master, where is my fear?

1.5.3.en: Saith the LORD of hosts unto you, O priests, that despise my name.

1.5.4.en: And ye say, Wherein have we despised thy name? [6]

1.5.5.en: By the law of nature a son honors his father, and by the laws of the world a servant fears his master, obeys his commands and is careful to serve his interests. The son who does not honor his father falls under the curse of natural law, and the servant who does not listen to his master falls under the penalty of the laws of society. This is the position of the son and the servant; so what is the position of the priest, who is governed by the divine law? Which has the greater claim to obedience, the divine law or the laws of nature and society?

1.5.6.en: If the priest desires to be called a father (Judg 18:19), and if some look to him as a leader whom they must obey, then the priest must deal with God as a son and a servant of His. For how can the priest call the people to honor God as a Father, and to submit to Him as a Master, when he does not bear the same spirit? St. Paul says: "Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?" (Heb 12:9).

1.5.7.en: * God asks of all creatures: "If then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear?" (Mal 1:6). If human life has no master to oversee it, it turns into a chaos that calls for lamentation. This is what became of the heavenly powers that rebelled and stiffened their necks against God the Almighty, refusing to submit to Him, not because they were of an uncreated nature, but because the cause of their disobedience was rebellion against the Creator.

1.5.8.en: * It is said: "A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master" (Mal 1:6). Of these two, servitude is offered by the creature, and the other, which may be called intimate friendship, is accomplished by the Holy Spirit.

1.5.9.en: St. Basil the Great * Our prayer must agree with the "good" will of the One to whom we pray, by glorifying Him in the opening of the prayer. That is why we were commanded to begin with nothing but the words "Our Father which art in heaven."

1.5.10.en: Indeed many words concerning the glorification of God are spread through the pages of the Holy Scripture, but we never found a commandment for the people of the Jews to say "Our Father," that is, they did not pray to Him as sons but as servants, as those who still lived according to the flesh.

1.5.11.en: I say that they did not take God as their Father, though they could have done so had they not disobeyed the Law they were commanded to keep. Therefore the following texts came:

1.5.12.en: "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" (Isa 1:2).

1.5.13.en: "I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High" (Ps 82:6).

1.5.14.en: "If then I be a father, where is mine honour... etc." (Mal 1:6)

1.5.15.en: These texts show that they were not accepted as sons of God, and they are also a prophecy of what Christians would be, who take God as their Father, as the Evangelist says: "But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God" (Jn 1:12). And as the Apostle Paul says: "The heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant" (Gal 4:1), pointing to the spirit of adoption which we have received, by which we cry, "Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15).

1.5.16.en: St. Augustine * The glory of fathers is the holiness of their sons, and the honor of masters is the fear of their servants, while the opposite brings insult and confusion. For He says: "Because of you My name is blasphemed among the Gentiles."

1.5.17.en: The Didascalia * "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" (Isa 1:2)... He does not point to their fellowship with all mankind in expressions of the loftiness of their birth, but rather to a surpassing help in that they became His sons. God takes the initiative in every matter by giving gifts. In the creation of man He began by honoring him even before He brought him into being, saying: "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness" (Gen 1:26)... Here one can see that God honors the adoption of man.

1.5.18.en: * Those who have become sons and enjoy the spiritual food have the right to glorify their Father. The Scripture says: "A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master." You have become His son and you enjoy the spiritual food; you receive His Body and Blood, which give you a new birth. Therefore, repay such a kindness by glorifying the One who gave it to you. And when you read these words, make sure of your attachment to them. When he says: "I will extol thee, my God, O king" (Ps 145:1), give testimony of your intimate relationship, so that God may say of you, as of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob" (Ex 3:6). I mean, if you say, "My God, my King," and not only say this but also give testimony of such love, He in turn says the same thing about you: "My servant, My companion," which He said also of Moses.

1.5.19.en: * He who has the fear is not meddlesome, but falls down and worships. He who has the fear does not raise questions out of curiosity, but on the contrary offers praise and glory.

1.5.20.en: St. John Chrysostom * Last week I spoke at sufficient length for the correction of those who do not give thanks to the Creator for the divine gifts they enjoy, those who, while benefiting from heavenly tenderness, as ungrateful and unworthy people do not know the giver of the tenderness. They are ungrateful, I say, those who do not fear God as servants toward their master, nor honor Him as sons toward their father. God says through the prophet: "If I be a master, where is my fear? and if I be a father, where is mine honour?" (Mal 1:6), meaning: if you are a servant, offer service to the Master with fear, and if you are a son, show your father reverent love. But since you do not give thanks, you neither love God nor fear Him. You are an arrogant servant or a proud son. The good Christian must praise his Father and Master continually, and practice all good works for His glory. This is as the Apostle says: "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God" (1 Cor 10:33).

1.5.21.en: Maximus, bishop of Turin * Concerning God, who is one alone, bearing a person with two aspects as Father and Master, we are bound to love Him since we are His sons, and to fear Him since we are His servants.

1.5.22.en: Lactantius * This fear or love for which God rebukes us, each one according to what suits him, saying: "A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear?" (Mal 1:6). For the servant must fear: "And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes" (Lk 12:47).

1.5.23.en: * There is a twofold fear: 1. One is for beginners, that is, those who are still under the terrifying bondage, of which we read: "a servant his master" (Mal 1:6). And in the Gospel He says: "Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth" (Jn 15:15). "And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Son abideth ever" (Jn 8:35). Therefore God teaches us to pass from the fear of punishment to the fullness of the freedom of love and the confidence of the beloved sons of God. Finally, the blessed Apostle, by the power of God's love, passed through the stage of the bondage of fear, so that he might despise earthly things and declare that he had been enriched with the good things of God, when he says: "For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind" (2 Tim 1:7). To those too who are kindled with perfect love toward their heavenly Father, and who through divine adoption have become sons and not servants, the Apostle says: "For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15). 2. As for the other fear, the prophet speaks of the sevenfold Spirit, who according to the mystery of the Incarnation rests in fullness upon the incarnate God: "And the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD" (Isa 11:2). And he adds in particular: "And his delight shall be in the fear of the LORD" (Isa 11:3). We notice that he did not go on to say, "the spirit of fear shall rest upon You," but "his delight shall be in the fear of the LORD." For this is the greatness and the wealth of this fear, that when it settles upon someone with its power it does not take possession of a part of his mind but of all his mind. And this is not without understanding, for it is closely bound to love, which "never faileth."

1.5.24.en: Father Chaeremon A grave accusation is directed at the people as well as the priests, and a grave answer: "Wherein have we despised thy name?" It brings us before a sad and terrifying picture.

1.5.25.en: The gravest thing in the matter is the spiritual blindness that struck them all, so that they did not feel that they were despising God's name; perhaps they even boasted that they offered offerings and sacrifices and practiced worship with exactness according to the Law.

1.5.26.en: The Jewish people prided themselves on having the tribe of Levi, from whom came the priests whom the Lord had chosen for Himself, who offered sacrifices and offerings that were pleasing to God. Now God Himself reveals to them that the priests who intercede for them to obtain blessings had lost the blessing, the holiness and God's good pleasure. Who then can lift up the face of the people before God?

1.5.27.en: God speaks through the prophet to call the priests to account. If they were appointed judges in the house of the Lord, it was so that they themselves might first practice the commandment and live it, or else fall under judgment.

1.5.28.en: * Be obedient to your bishop; obey him as your spiritual father. Sons love, and servants fear. He says: "If then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear?" (Mal 1:6). In your case, one person may bear many labors for your honor, being at the same time a monk, a bishop and an uncle. But bishops must know that they are priests and not lords. Let them restore to the priesthood the honor that befits it.

1.5.29.en: St. Jerome * This is your duty, O bishop: not to ignore the sins of the people, and not to reject those who are repentant, lest you break the Lord's flock through lack of skill, or insult His new name which has been placed upon a people, while you yourself are rebuked as happened with the ancient shepherds of whom God said to Jeremiah: "Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot" (Jer 12:10). And in another passage: "My anger was kindled against the shepherds, and My wrath against the lambs" (cf. Zech 10:3). And in another place: "O priests, that despise my name" (Mal 1:6).

1.5.30.en: * It is clear that the bishops and priests who are thus called in vain do not escape God's judgment.

1.6.0.en: 7 Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar; and ye say, Wherein have we polluted thee? In that ye say, The table of the LORD is contemptible. 8 And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil? offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the LORD of hosts. 9 And now, I pray you, beseech God that he will be gracious unto us: this hath been by your means: will he regard your persons? saith the LORD of hosts.

1.6.1.en: Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar.

1.6.2.en: And ye say, Wherein have we polluted thee?

1.6.3.en: In that ye say, The table of the LORD is contemptible. [7]

1.6.4.en: The accusation He directs against the priests is the despising of God's name and the defiling of His holy things. What is graver than this is that when they hear the accusation they answer: "Wherein have we despised thy name? Wherein have we polluted thee?" Such questions reveal either the priests' ignorance of the truth, which is a grave matter since they are blind leaders leading the people, or their knowledge of what they are doing, so that they answer with a measure of unseemly boldness, and this is worse! Their committing evil, whether knowingly or unknowingly, is extremely grave by reason of their position of leadership.

1.6.5.en: "The table of the LORD is contemptible": perhaps this means the table of the showbread or the altar of burnt offerings. It was called this because the priests and the people ate from it, as though God, who accepts the sacrifices, wished the priests and the people to share with Him as at a table of reconciliation.

1.7.0.en: By their sharing in the sacrifices offered to idols they despise the table of the Lord, since they wish for fellowship with God and the idols, or with God and Satan. By this they are counted as those who have polluted the table of the Lord [12].

1.7.1.en: They despised the table of the Lord by offering defective sacrifices, giving the first place to themselves and counting God unworthy to be offered the best of what they had.

1.7.2.en: They offered sacrifices on the table of the Lord, or the altar, and thought they were pleasing Him, not realizing that they were despising Him and polluting His altar. Therefore they ask: "Wherein have we polluted thee?" They offered sacrifices, but their hearts were far from the Lord, and opposed to Him, not accepting His commandment and not wishing to enjoy fellowship with Him.

1.7.3.en: And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil?

1.7.4.en: And if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil?

1.7.5.en: Offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the LORD of hosts. [8]

1.7.6.en: They offered the sacrifices that were fit for no other purpose, reckoning that any burnt offering is burned with fire, so they grudged offering animals that were fit for sale or trade or any other purpose, as though they were offering God their leftovers. In the Book of Deuteronomy it says concerning sacrifices: "And if there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame, or blind, or have any ill blemish, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the LORD thy God. Thou shalt eat it within thy gates: the unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike, as the roebuck, and as the hart" (Deut 15:21-22).

1.7.7.en: The sacrifice of the blind refers to practicing worship without spiritual benefit, so that we are like one who performs a duty in ignorance, without looking to God to learn His joyful heavenly mysteries.

1.7.8.en: The sacrifice of the lame refers to the person who does not enjoy the Lord Christ as the divine Way by which he goes forth toward the Father's bosom, so that his soul may be settled, rest and be comforted by the heavenly Father.

1.7.9.en: The sacrifice of the sick refers to the one who practices worship with indifference, without fixing his eyes on the Lord, the heavenly Physician, so that his sick soul stands still without seeking true healing.

1.7.10.en: It is to be noted in the three preceding sacrifices, whether that of the blind, the lame or the sick, that man practices his worship with the body and not the heart, with the letter and not the spirit, so that he carries a heart without enlightenment, without spiritual movement, and in slackness!

1.7.11.en: He reproaches them that what they practice in their relationship with Him they would not dare to do with a king or governor whose favor they seek, since they could not offer a gift or tribute with a lame animal or a crooked one.

1.7.12.en: * So was the offering of Cain the murderer rejected. God said to him: "If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?" (Gen 4:7). So also were all the offerings of Israel rejected, so that they received the curse that the prophet spoke: "But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing" (Mal 1:14). He rebukes and reproves them, saying: "Offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or show thee tenderness? saith the LORD" (cf. Mal 1:8). How then can any speech directed to God during the service of prayer, showing any kind of disrespect, be acceptable to God, a speech full of every kind of distraction, that is, a sick speech hindered by many interruptions (through distraction of thought)? Such a kind would not be acceptable even if offered to the most insignificant human being if addressed to him in this way. A prayer offering full of disturbance and the service of a careless heart are like the sacrifice of a ram that is wholly defective.

1.7.13.en: Observe with us: if God takes no pleasure in sacrifice and offering (Ps 40:6), but seeks sacrifices of praise, thanksgiving and gratitude (Ps 51:16; 116:17; Jer 33:11), then He accepts them from pure, holy lips, but whoever offers them from unclean lips, which curse and do not bless, lie and do not speak the truth, judge and do not show mercy, his are counted unclean sacrifices. It is as though the man were offering the sacrifice of the blind, the lame or the sick.

1.7.14.en: And now, I pray you, beseech God that he will be gracious unto us.

1.7.15.en: This hath been by your means.

1.7.16.en: Will he regard your persons? saith the LORD of hosts. [9]

1.7.17.en: Some see that a plague came upon the land, when raids of locusts attacked the fields and ate what was green (Mal 3:11), and the priests cried out but the Lord did not answer because of their wickedness. Therefore He gives them the counsel to return to God in repentance and He will hear their prayers, for themselves as well as for the people. As the psalmist says: "If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me" (Ps 66:18).

1.7.18.en: * Return to yourself; be a judge for yourself within. Look at your hidden chamber, in the depths of the heart, there where you and God who sees are alone together, and do not take pleasure in iniquity, and God will take pleasure in you... "But verily God hath heard me" (Ps 66:19), because I do not regard iniquity in my heart, "he hath attended to the voice of my prayer" (Ps 66:19). "Blessed be God, which hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me" (Ps 66:20).

1.7.19.en: St. Augustine "This hath been by your means" [9], meaning that God wishes to hear the prayers of His priests on behalf of their people, but because of their iniquity He does not hear them until they return to Him.

1.8.0.en: 10 Who is there even among you that would shut the doors for nought? neither do ye kindle fire on mine altar for nought. I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. 11 For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts.

1.8.1.en: Who is there even among you that would shut the doors for nought? neither do ye kindle fire on mine altar for nought.

1.8.2.en: I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. [10]

1.8.3.en: With complete frankness the Lord, the God of hosts, declares: "I have no pleasure in you," showing that with the love with which He loved them He loves all mankind. And in the clearness of day He shines with His sun upon all the nations that offer fragrant incense to the glory of His holy name.

1.8.4.en: The priests thought that they were opening the doors of the temple and kindling the altar, but since they behaved as hirelings seeking material gain for themselves, the divine voice came to them: "I have no pleasure in you." He who loves them, assuring them: "I have loved you" [2], tells them that He has no pleasure in them. It is deeply regrettable! God no longer has pleasure in the service of these priests who practice worship only for the sake of pay; whether they shut the door or kindle a fire or do any work, they demand pay! As it is written in the prophet Isaiah: "Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his shameful gain" (Isa 56:11).

1.8.5.en: God has allowed those who serve at the altar to eat from the altar, and those who serve the Gospel to eat from the Gospel (1 Cor 9:7-14), but they do not work with a view to pay and shameful gain.

1.8.6.en: God calls us to review our depths so that we may touch the hidden motive of our worship of Him, our service and our preaching.

1.8.7.en: * Malachi, the last of all the prophets, speaks with all frankness about the rejection of Israel and the calling of the Gentiles.

1.8.8.en: St. Jerome * The Jews returned from Babylon, repaired the city, rebuilt the temple, and offered sacrifices. But before everything the prophet Malachi prophesied of the present desolation that was to come and of the abomination of the Jewish sacrifices.

1.8.9.en: * Do you not see how he stops the Jewish ways and abolishes them, and spreads the way of life of the Church and proclaims its worship?

1.8.10.en: St. John Chrysostom * You, O Jew, have not come to a pure sacrifice; I will prove to you that it is not pure.

1.8.11.en: * Why do you try, O Jews, to twist these prophetic words to another meaning as your heart dictates? You oppose the Son of God against your own salvation... For the house of Jacob or Israel is the very same people who were called and who were cast out; it was not called with respect to some and cast out with respect to others, but the whole house is called to walk in the light of the Lord... The reason for casting out the house is that its people did not walk in the light of the Lord.

1.8.12.en: St. Augustine * If a man is a Scythian or a Persian, if he has the knowledge of God and the knowledge of His Christ, and keeps the ordinances of eternal righteousness, he is circumcised with the good and profitable circumcision, and he is a friend of God, and God rejoices in his gifts and offerings...

1.9.0.en: St. Justin Martyr For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts. [11]

1.9.1.en: In the Old Testament the hymn was: "In Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel" (Ps 76:1). Now all the nations glorify Him, from the rising of the sun to its going down.

1.9.2.en: * Now I return to Malachi. This man prophesied about the Church, which spread by the power of Christ and widened greatly, and he spoke to the Jews on God's lips: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts" (Mal 1:10-11). Now if we see that in this our time, in every place from the rising of the sun to its going down, this sacrifice is offered according to the order of Melchizedek, and if the Jews cannot in any circumstances deny that their sacrifices are rejected... how can they await the coming of another Christ? They read the prophecy, and see its fulfillment before their eyes. Why can they not verify that the One who fulfills this is the Christ, since no other can do it?

1.9.3.en: St. Augustine * He speaks of these Gentiles, that is, of us, who offer sacrifices to Him in every place, that is, the bread of the Eucharist and also the cup of the Eucharist, each affirming that we glorify His name while you defile it.

1.9.4.en: * God announced beforehand all the sacrifices that we offer in His name, which Jesus Christ commanded us to offer, that is, the Eucharist of the bread and the cup, which Christians offer in every place in the world, bearing witness that they are pleasing to Him. But He utterly rejects what you offer and what your priests offer.

1.9.5.en: St. Justin Martyr * The Creator of all things, his Counselor, asked his only-begotten Son to come down from heaven and turn the holy faith in God to the Gentiles, that is, to those who were ignorant of God, and to teach them the righteousness which the treacherous people had cast away from them. He had long before threatened them that He would do this, as Malachi shows.

1.9.6.en: Lactantius * These words indicate in a clear way that the former people [the Jews] cease the offerings to God, but in every place a pure sacrifice is offered to Him, and His name is glorified among the Gentiles.

1.9.7.en: St. Irenaeus * In place of the bloody sacrifice He appoints a mystical, rational, bloodless sacrifice, that of His Body and Blood, which is carried out to represent the death of the Lord... In place of the divine service limited to one place, He commands and appoints that His authority be glorified from the east to the west in every place (Ps 13:3; Mal 1:11). By this He did not abolish the Law but abolished the restrictions.

1.9.8.en: The Didascalia * When Abraham returned from the defeat of his enemies, Melchizedek, priest of the most high God, met him with bread and wine. That table had already prefigured this mystical table. And that priest was a type and image of Christ, the true Great High Priest, for the prophet says: "Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek" (Ps 110:4). And the loaves of the offering, which were an image of this bread, are therefore the pure, that is, bloodless sacrifice of which the Lord spoke by the prophet's tongue: it is offered to Him from the rising of the sun to its going down (Mal 1:11).

1.9.9.en: Father John of Damascus * Now concerning the place, let it be known that every place is suitable for prayer if a man prays well! For the Lord says: "In every place incense shall be offered unto my name" (Mal 1:11), and "I will therefore that men pray every where" (1 Tim 2:8). But let each one, if I may put it so, have if possible a chosen holy place in his house to perform his prayers in quiet without distraction.

1.9.10.en: Origen * Surely the Lord gives authority to pray in every place, in the words: "Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father" (Jn 4:21). And the words of the Apostle are lawful (2 Tim 2:8). For the word "every" does not include places set apart for human use or for defiled, disgraceful works, but it removes the limits of Jerusalem to other places in the world set apart as is fitting (for worship), in harmony with the prophecy about the sacrifice (Mal 1:11).

1.9.11.en: They are consecrated to God for the celebration of the glorious mystery.

1.9.12.en: St. Basil the Great * Since circumcision and uncircumcision belong to the one God, both have been made void in Christ because of the priority given to faith. This is the faith of which it is written that in His name shall the Gentiles trust (Isa 42:4; Mt 12:21).

1.9.13.en: Tertullian * When the only-begotten Son came, His name became wonderful in every place... Another writer says: The whole world is filled with the knowledge of the Lord (Isa 11:9).

1.9.14.en: * When do you think this happened, O Jews? When was incense offered to God in every place? When was a pure offering offered? You cannot point to any other time except after the coming of Christ. Suppose Malachi did not speak of our age, suppose he did not speak of our sacrifice but of the Jewish sacrifice, then his prophecy would be contrary to the Law. For Moses forbade the Jews to offer their sacrifice in any place other than the one the Lord God chose, for he limited their sacrifices to one appointed place. So if Malachi said that sacrifices are offered in every place, and that it should be a pure sacrifice, he contradicts and opposes what Moses said.
